threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still check the tube line status before leaving home—true locals know it's a gamble regardless.
Last night on the 196, a guy tried to sell a lost cat collar to everyone. Claimed it was 'vintage.' You can't make this stuff up.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a street artist painting a mural of a cat on a traffic light while someone tried to sell homemade lemonade from a bicycle. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop open at 3 AM with a line longer than a club's. It's the unofficial after-party scene, just with more tahini.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from the Mission when they can name three taquerias just from the scent of grilled onions wafting by.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: The Muni bus departed while a jogger tried to catch it—no sprinting. They stopped to catch their breath and kept running, like it was all just a part of the routine.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: They think Gràcia is all about the Gaudí and the parks, but it’s really the hidden plazas and local bars that have the heart of the neighborhood.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by the way they still take photos of the Diagonal’s traffic lights—like it’s some hidden gem, not just another boring crosswalk.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it ‘the tube’ instead of ‘the Overground’—that’s a sure sign you’re new to Dalston.
The 196 night bus pulled up and a guy stepped off with a full suit and a pineapple. No idea where he was headed, but it made the whole stop pause.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I lived here when the kebab shop owner started recommending his favorite wine to me. It's the little things, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, you can enjoy spontaneous street performances paired with currywurst at midnight, a blend of culture and culinary that's uniquely Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they know to bring a sweater, even in summer—Fog City is real, and the weather is a constant surprise.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy lecturing tourists on Muni etiquette while waiting for the 21. Call me crazy, but it felt like prime Tenderloin performance art.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always stop for ice cream at Joan Blanques, not realizing the best scoop is at the tiny gelateria on Carrer de l’Escorial. It's a local secret.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell the newcomers—they're the ones still looking at maps trying to figure out which way is east when the sun’s setting.
